Long English-only stretch 09:14-20:20 on Amal's proposed non-human-plural-as-feminine rule; his 'الدروس صعبات, right?' (11:57), 'باردات؟' (11:38), 'kabirat?' (16:10) are QUESTIONS about a rule she said 'we're not learning it' - not filed. Echo: '12:24 reduce بدت' = his repeat of الدروس بدت. Latin stretches 23:52-24:10 and 28:41-29:07 (inbastatish t-mashing = pronunciation, S4, not filed). 20:33 behkesh->behkish is his own self-fix before her. 07:24/07:33 هذه = engine spelling of hadi, not filed. 07:40 الجو شمس she typed shams herself - not filed. 24:18 من إشي ثاني vs her chat min ay ishi taani - not filed. Few rows because the lesson is ~29 min and mostly English talk about rules.

rows.amal_said: No. You're a key. You can't open.
rows.why: He reached for 'relaxed' and said مفتوح / مفتاح (open / key); Amal said No, you're a key, and he then found مرتاح (her chat ana mertaa7).

rows.medi_said: اشتغلت، اه بيتي. من بيتي؟ لا، اشتغلت بيتي.
rows.why: He floated من بيتي then rejected it ('لا، اشتغلت بيتي'); Amal said Yes, صح، من بيتي - the preposition min is needed.

rows.chat: ijtimaa3i el-a5eer / aa5er ijtimaa3 ili kaan 3ala el-wa7de
rows.why: For 'my last meeting' he put aa5er on a plural with a possessive ending (= the last of my meetings / end of); Amal prompted ('Did you add in?', 'It's one. اجتماع.') and typed aa5er ijtimaa3 / ijtimaa3i el-a5eer.

rows.medi_said: الأخيرة. / It's right. اجتماعات الأخيرة، right?
rows.amal_said: No، اجتماع is masculine. ... You don't need a t.
rows.why: He put the feminine adjective الأخيرة on اجتماع; Amal said No, اجتماع is masculine, you don't need a t, and he then said اجتماعي الأخير.
Clock time needs el-: he said على واحد / واحدة, Amal recast الوحدة and he repeated الواحدة (her chat 3ala el-wa7de).

rows.chat: shu el-yoam yoam el-5amees, 5amse e7da3sh alfain u sitte u 3eshreen
rows.why: In a date the number stands alone and keeps its -e (5amse); Amal said No, he fixed to خمسة, and she then asked when the number drops its ending (only when counting a noun).
Clock time takes the feminine number (tentain); he said اثنين, Amal let it pass in voice and only typed tentain illa tult (chat alone is not a correction, GR-19).
He understood her هذي الفترة as 'at this moment'; Amal said No and repeated it, and he then worked out فترة = this period of time.
Same rule as 06:25: a bare number keeps its -e (5amse u sitteen); Amal said No, مش خمس.

After the Arabic number failed he said English 'sixteen' (sheet: 'sixteen | sitta3sh | ستاعش', 'sixty | sittin | ستين'); her chat shows he meant 65 - pre-ruled tier-3 let-pass (AR-1933); may be the engine for 'sixty-'.

rows.medi_said: Is it بعيد؟ بعيد becomes bad?
rows.why: He heard her بدت and guessed it came from بعيد (far); Amal said no, it is from بدا (started).

rows.amal_said: That's I don't miss. I don't complain.
rows.why: Asked for 'I don't complain' he said بشتاقش (I don't miss), a different verb; Amal said that's I don't miss and he switched to بشكيش (sheet: complain | Eshki | اشتكي).

rows.amal_said: مهم. Where's the t؟ You keep the t.
rows.chat: ma / tenze3jesh min ay ishi taani
rows.why: A negative command is built on the you-form with its t- prefix; he said زعجش with no t, Amal said Where's the t? You keep the t.

rows.chat: ma / tenze3jesh min ay ishi taani
rows.why: He used the za3aj (annoy someone) stem instead of the n- form inza3aj (get annoyed); Amal said Again, he reached بنزعج, she confirmed 'بنزعج، صح' and he noted 'There's an N'.

rows.chat: ma / tenze3jesh min ay ishi taani
rows.why: After her t fix he dropped the t- again (انزعجش, past/command stem); Amal said la, it doesn't work, تنزعجش - its own slip after the fix (GR-32).

rows.amal_said: About anything else. ... هيك issue something like this.
rows.chat: ma / tenze3jesh min ay ishi taani
rows.right: من إشي ثاني (min ay ishi taani)
rows.why: For 'about anything else' he said min heik (from this / like this); Amal repeated 'About anything else' twice and said heik is 'something like this', then he said من إشي ثاني.
He asked how to say 'too much'; Amal pointed him to 'Extra' (sheet: extra / increase | Ziaadeh | زيادة), which he then used.
In the -ish negation drill he left the -ish off; Amal said No, Where's your ish? (again at 26:05) until he said ما تنبسطيش; no bucket covers the -ish negative.
rows.proposed_rule: A negative verb or command can take -ish at the end (bahkeesh, ma tenze3jesh, tenbestish); in Amal's ish drill the verb must carry -ish, with or without ma.

rows.why: He said زياد (a man's name) for زيادة; Amal echoed 'Zia' and he completed زيـ زيادة - may just be a cut-off word (S5).
Same t- drop she fixed at 23:04 and 23:40 (negative command needs the you-form t-); here she let it pass in voice and only typed tenbestish.
